task.title: Assembly
task.shortdesc: It is finally time to start connecting components

taskbody.context:
You should never force any components together. All connectors are keyed to only go together one way, and will eventually snap together with moderate pressure. Getting them apart again usually involves lifting a latch or tab and can be quite difficult.
Turn off the PSU and unplug the cable from the socket before adjusting any cabling or components. Never install or remove any component while the PSU is connected to the wall outlet.

step.cmd: First install the CPU into the socket on the motherboard according to the CPU instructions.

substep.cmd: Do not force the CPU into the socket. If it doesn’t settle in with light pressure check the alignment of the CPU with socket and try again.
If it still doesn’t settle in re-verify you have the right type of motherboard socket for your CPU.

step.cmd: Build the clips for the cooler around the CPU socket.

substep.cmd: If you have an M.2 SSD storage device now is the best time to install it into the motherboard. This kind of device connects directly to the motherboard, and as more components are added it will be harder to get your hands in there.

step.cmd: Install the motherboard into the case.

substep.cmd: Carefully align the holes in the motherboard with the holes in the case.
Place screws in an X pattern, starting from the corners and working inwards. After placing one screw place the next on the opposite corner. Do not tighten until all screws are placed.
Gently tighten screws in the same X pattern, again starting from the corners and working inwards.
Do not overtighten the screws. This can damage the motherboard.

step.cmd: Instal the PSU, but do NOT plug it in yet.
Carefully install the GPU, RAM, and any other cards into their respective slots.

substep.cmd: Do not use excessive force. All components should slot into place with steady medium pressure.
Ensure the clips that hold the RAM cards in place are snug. Improperly slotted RAM can damage the RAM and cause the system to not boot up.

step.cmd: Install fans into the case if they did not already come screwed in.

ol.li: Intake fans should be on the front of the case
Exhaust fans should be on the rear of the case
The difference between an intake fan and an exhaust fan is usually just orientation. There is an arrow on the fan to indicate airflow direction.

step.cmd: Connect case fans, lights, and any other peripherals to the motherboard.
Connect the PSU to the motherboard, GPU, and any other peripherals.

substep.cmd: Double check the PSU is turned off and unplugged before connecting or disconnecting any cables.
All power cables should snap into place with firm, medium pressure.

step.cmd: Finish installing the heatsink and cooler according to their directions.

substep.cmd: You only need a pea sized amount of thermal paste for the heatsink.
I save this step for last because the cooler will block access to a large section of the motherboard and make connecting any cables much more difficult.
Zip ties or twist ties work to keep cables secured.
In particular make sure cable are clear of any fans.
